name: Darnford Albion

location.about: A town of about 120,000 on the south bank of the river, facing Riverton across a dozen bridges: maltings and breweries, the canal port and the railway works. Always the smaller of the two - and always trying to prove it isn't.

colours.story: Amber and black - the colours of the malt kilns, said the founders, men from the Trent Bank maltings who started the club in 1883 to give Riverton a game.

rivals.why: the city across the river - a dozen bridges and one long grudge, since the first derby in 1884
Founders' Cup finals a hundred years apart - 1923 and 2023 - and Darnford won both

history.title: Across the river
history.text: Founded in 1883 by men from the maltings; the first Trent Derby a year later. Beaten in three Founders' Cup finals (1897, 1901, 1911), Second Division champions in 1900 - and in 1912 second, to Riverton of all clubs. Three years later, the last season before the war, champions of England: 1915.

history.title: A cup side
history.text: The Founders' Cup in 1923 (against Kingsmere), lost the 1925 final to Oakhurst, won again in 1930 (Northwick) and lost in 1934. Second in 1938 behind Millbrook - and relegated in 1948, after the war. Second Division champions in 1949; the Founders' Cup in 1952 against Eastvale.

history.title: The long fade
history.text: The Founders' Cup in 1965 against Bramhall - and then nothing much: Charter Cup finals lost in 1971 and 1982, relegation, promotion in 1978, relegation again. Riverton's fans called the bridges 'the way to the Second Division'.

history.title: Up and down the bridges
history.text: Division 1 champions in 2003; beaten in the 2004 Charter Cup final; down, and back up as runners-up in 2006. The Charter Cup in 2008 against Eastvale. Down again - and up through the play-offs in 2011, the same spring Riverton went down. Up again as runners-up in 2015.

history.title: The best years since 1915
history.text: 2022 was the season of the club's life: the Charter Cup won as a Division 1 side (against Quarrington, in the first all-Division 1 final) and promotion through the play-offs a month later. A year on, back in the Premier Division, the Founders' Cup against Kingsmere - a hundred years after the first.

honours_note: League seasons are given by the year they ended (1915 = 1914-15).

legends.name: Walter Pask
legends.note: Maltster; captained the side in the first Trent Derby.

legends.name: Cyril Gotheridge
legends.note: 193 goals - the club record; scored twice in the 1930 final.

legends.name: Kevin Dunmore
legends.note: The 2022 Charter Cup, promotion, and the 2023 Founders' Cup.

legends.name: Tunde Bakare
legends.note: Scored in both the 2022 and 2023 finals.

records.attendance: 47,920 v Riverton Dynamo, League, 1938 (Trent Bank, before seating)
records.defeat: 0-10 v Ashvale Rovers, League, 1892 and v Eastvale Wanderers, League, 1906

badge.about: A malt kiln's cowl and the bridge over the river - Darnford's side of it. Motto 'Ultra Pontem' - beyond the bridge.
badge.design: An amber circle with a black ring. In the centre a black stone bridge of three arches over wavy black water, and above it the pointed cowl of an old malt kiln. 'DARNFORD ALBION' in amber capitals around the black ring, '1883' at the bottom.

ground.name: Trent Bank

stands.name: Maltings Stand
stands.features: the main stand, in front of the old maltings (now flats): tunnel, dugouts, boxes

stands.name: Bridge End
stands.features: the home end - from the top row you can see Riverton's floodlights across the river

stands.name: Canal Stand
stands.features: a long single tier along the canal towpath

ground.surroundings: the river and its bridges right behind the home end, Riverton's floodlights and towers on the far bank, malt kilns with pointed cowls, a canal basin with narrowboats, the railway station
ground.atmosphere: tight and loud - and on derby days the most hostile ground in the Midlands
